Wloszczowa Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Włoszczowa, Poland

Demolished. Włoszczowa, granted town rights in 1539 and a noted Calvinist center by the 17th century, saw its Jewish community develop mainly from the second half of the 18th century, likely subordinate to the communities of Przedbórz or Chęciny; by 1872, Jews made up 64 percent of the population. During WWII, the Germans established a ghetto and forced labor camp, deporting most Jews to Treblinka in fall 1942 and several hundred more to the Sandomierz labor camp, with several hundred additional murders carried out directly at the town's newer Jewish cemetery, documented elsewhere in this collection. This older cemetery, most likely established in the first half of the 18th century, was probably used only until the mid-19th century — community records from 1904 and 1935 mention only the newer cemetery — before its final destruction during WWII.
